title: Stable genus and smooth-family open loci in curve families
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $g\geq2$. Let $\mathfrak C$ be the stack of flat proper finitely presented families of algebraic spaces with geometric fibres of dimension at most one. For every such family $X\to T$, there is an open subscheme $T_g^{\mathrm{st}}\subset T$, commuting with arbitrary base change, characterized by the following property: a morphism $T'\to T$ factors through it exactly when $X_{T'}\to T'$ is an unpointed stable genus-$g$ curve with the projective-bundle convention and component stability condition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. In particular, over this open, the algebraic space $X$ is a scheme and the family has a closed embedding into the projective bundle of a finite-rank locally free module on its base. The corresponding full subcategory is an open substack of $\mathfrak C$, contained in its nodal substack. There is also a base-change-compatible open subscheme $T^{\mathrm{sm}}\subset T$ characterized by smoothness of the whole family after pullback [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tags 0E76 (lemma-stable-curves), 0E78 (lemma-stable-one-piece-per-genus), and the smooth-family open in lemma-smooth-dense (Tag 0E86); scheme/projective-bundle comparison uses the relatively ample dualizing sheaf in the stable-family discussion preceding 0E76 and its pluricanonical embedding. The projective-bundle formulation for arbitrary bases is the agent expansion of this comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-curve-stack-smooth] to the classifying map of $X/T$. The current statement defines its nodal substack by nonempty pure one-dimensional geometric fibres with at worst ordinary nodes and explicitly imposes no connectedness. Its stated open-substack test gives an open pullback $N\subset T$. Pulling back this defining square along $T'\to T$ identifies the new nodal open with $T'\times_TN$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-h0-genus-strata] to $X_N/N$: intersect $N$ with its scalar-$H^0$ open and then with the rank-$g$ open-and-closed stratum for $R^1f_*\mathcal O$. Call the resulting open $P$. Nodal fibres are geometrically reduced; the same cohomological lemma identifies the scalar-$H^0$ condition with geometric connectedness. Thus $P$ is characterized, after any base change, by connected nonempty nodal geometric fibres of arithmetic genus $g$. All three open constructions commute with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tags 0E6U (lemma-prestable-curves), 0E6V (lemma-prestable-one-piece-per-genus); nodal reducedness from 0E37, included in the cited dualizing-line statement.

proof.text: On $X_P/P$ use [lem-sfb-nodal-relative-dualizing-line] to obtain the canonical line $\omega$, whose pullback to each geometric fibre is its dualizing line and whose formation commutes with every base change. For a geometric fibre $C$, apply [lem-sfb-nodal-canonical-positivity-tricanonical]. Its equivalence says exactly that $\omega_C$ is ample when and only when the genus-zero component normalizations have at least three branches over nodes and the genus-one normalizations have at least one. There are no markings. These are precisely the component inequalities of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve] for zero sections; their genera are the dimensions of $H^1$ on the smooth proper normalized components.

source.place: Tag 0E74 (lemma-stable), interpreted with component normalizations; Tag 0E6R for the relative line.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ample-locus] to $X_P\to P$ and $\omega$. It yields an open $A\subset P$ characterized universally by relative ampleness of $\omega$. Set $T_g^{\mathrm{st}}=A$, viewed as an open of $T$. Its geometric points are, by the preceding fibre criterion, exactly the connected nodal genus-$g$ fibres with the required component inequalities. The ample-locus statement gives that $X_A$ is a scheme. Both the formation of $P$ and the dualizing-line identification commute with base change, and the ample-locus universal property therefore identifies the stable open after any $T'\to T$ with $T'\times_TA$.

source.place: Tag 0E76 (lemma-stable-curves), proof via canonical ampleness; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3D.

proof.text: Over $A$, take $L=\omega^{\otimes3}$. By [lem-sfb-nodal-canonical-positivity-tricanonical] every geometric fibre of $L$ is very ample and has vanishing $H^1$. The scheme family $X_A/A$ is still flat, proper and finitely presented with one-dimensional fibres. Thus [lem-sfb-fibrewise-very-ample-evaluation] gives a finite locally free module $E=f_*L$ and a closed embedding $X_A\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_A(E)$, compatible with all base changes. This supplies the projective-bundle convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve] without assuming the original space family was a scheme or projective, and without imposing a Noetherian or quasi-compact base.

source.place: Tag 0E8X (lemma-tricanonical), followed by the relative evaluation consequence of spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CTM.

proof.text: For a morphism $T'\to T$ factoring through $A$, steps 1--4 give a flat finitely presented projective-bundle scheme family, with connected nonempty reduced nodal geometric fibres of genus $g$ and the component inequalities. It is therefore an unpointed stable genus-$g$ family by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]. Conversely, such a family has nodal fibres and satisfies the scalar-$H^0$ and genus conditions, hence its base map factors through $P$ by the open descriptions in step 1. Its component inequalities imply ample dualizing geometric fibres, so the universal ample-locus description forces factorization through $A$. These implications use only the cited equivalences: no choice of an embedding is part of a stable-family object. The full subcategory has the same isomorphisms as $\mathfrak C$. Its 2-base change along any family over $T$ is the discrete fibred groupoid represented by $A\hookrightarrow T$ (the isomorphism to the given family is part of the 2-fibre product, so it removes its automorphisms). This is precisely the scheme-pullback test for an open substack stated in [lem-sfb-nodal-curve-stack-smooth]. It lies in the nodal substack since $A\subset N$.

source.place: Tags 0E76 and 0E78: universal interpretation and genus-$g$ open substack; the categorical conclusion is by the open-immersion test.

proof.text: For the smooth-family open, apply [lem-sfb-flat-space-smooth-locus] to the original flat finitely presented $f:X\to T$ and let $W\subset X$ be its smooth source locus. Put $Z=|X|\setminus|W|$ and $T^{\mathrm{sm}}=T\setminus f(Z)$. Properness includes universal closedness, so $f(Z)$ is closed. For any $h:T'\to T$, the cited source-locus theorem identifies the bad set of $f_{T'}$ with the inverse image $Z'$. Moreover $f_{T'}(Z')=h^{-1}(f(Z))$: for a point $t'$ over $t$, the bad fibre is empty exactly when the original bad fibre over $t$ is empty, since a nonempty fibre stays nonempty under a residue-field extension (choose a field-valued point and a prime of its nonzero tensor product with that extension). Hence the displayed complement is compatible with arbitrary base change, and $f_{T'}$ is smooth exactly when the image of $T'$ avoids $f(Z)$, equivalently when $h$ factors through $T^{\mathrm{sm}}$. No condition on the genus or connectedness is used for this open.

lean.statement: theorem stable_and_smooth_family_open_loci (k : Type u) [Field k] (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) : ∃ (stableOpen smoothOpen : (X : ProperCurveModuli (Spec (.of k))) → X.base.left.Opens), (∀ X : ProperCurveModuli (Spec (.of k)), (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (h : T ⟶ X.base), ((∃ l : T.left ⟶ (stableOpen X).toScheme, l ≫ (stableOpen X).ι = h.left) ↔ IsStableGenusSpaceFamily g T (Limits.pullback X.family.projection (yoneda.map h)) (Limits.pullback.snd X.family.projection (yoneda.map h)))) ∧ (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (h : T ⟶ X.base), ((∃ l : T.left ⟶ (smoothOpen X).toScheme, l ≫ (smoothOpen X).ι = h.left) ↔ ∀ (U : Over (Spec (.of k))) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Limits.pullback X.family.projection (yoneda.map h)), AlgebraicSpace.IsEtale a → Smooth ((yoneda.preimage (a ≫ Limits.pullback.snd X.family.projection (yoneda.map h))).left))) ∧ (∀ (Y : ProperCurveModuli (Spec (.of k))) (a : Y ⟶ X), stableOpen Y = a.base.left ⁻¹ᵁ stableOpen X ∧ smoothOpen Y = a.base.left ⁻¹ᵁ smoothOpen X) ∧ HasFiniteLocallyFreeProjectiveRealization (Over.mk ((stableOpen X).ι ≫ X.base.hom)) (Limits.pullback X.family.projection (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (stableOpen X).ι rfl : Over.mk ((stableOpen X).ι ≫ X.base.hom) ⟶ X.base))) (Limits.pullback.snd X.family.projection (yoneda.map (Over.homMk (stableOpen X).ι rfl : Over.mk ((stableOpen X).ι ≫ X.base.hom) ⟶ X.base)))) ∧ ∃ A : OpenModuliSubstack (ProperCurveModuli.category (Spec (.of k))), (∀ X : ProperCurveModuli (Spec (.of k)), A.property X ↔ IsStableGenusSpaceFamily g X.base X.family.space.obj.obj X.family.projection) ∧ (∀ X : ProperCurveModuli (Spec (.of k)), A.property X → X.family.HasNonemptyNodalGeometricFibres)
